# Ecclesiastes Chapter 8 -- The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** How wonderful it is to be wise and to be able to interpret the meaning of things. Wisdom makes a person's face light up, transforming a hard expression.

**2** Obey the king since you vowed before God that you would. **3** Don't try to avoid the king when he is displeased, and don't stand up for a bad cause, for the king does whatever he wants.

**4** His command is backed by great authority, and no one can say to him, "What are you doing?"

**5** Those who obey the king's commands will not get into trouble. Wise people will find the right time and the right way to act.

**6** Yes, there is a time and a way for everything, even when a person is in deep trouble.

**7** No one knows the future. Who can tell anyone what is going to happen?

**8** None of us can hold back our spirit from departing. None of us has the power to prevent the day of our death. There is no escaping that obligation, and evil will not rescue those who practice it.

**9** I have thought deeply about all that goes on here under the sun, where people exercise power over one another to their great hurt.

**10** I have seen wicked people buried with honor — people who used to go in and out of the temple and were praised in the very city where they did evil. How pointless!

**11** When a crime is not punished quickly, people feel it is safe to do wrong. **12** But even though a person sins a hundred times and still lives a long life, I know that those who fear God will be better off. **13** The wicked will not prosper, and their days will not last, for they do not fear God.

**14** And here is another problem with what happens on earth: good people are treated as though they were wicked, and wicked people are treated as though they were good. This is so pointless!

**15** So I recommend having fun, because there is nothing better for people in this world than to eat, drink, and enjoy life. That way they will experience some happiness along with all the hard work God gives them under the sun.

**16** I devoted myself to search for understanding and to observe people's never-ending activity — going without sleep day and night.

**17** Then I realized that no one can discover everything God is doing under the sun. No matter how hard they work at it, no one can figure it out. Even if the wisest person claims to know, they still can't really comprehend it.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**When crime goes unpunished (v.11):** This observation about delayed justice is startlingly modern. Qoheleth notices that when wrongdoers escape consequences, others are emboldened. This is not merely ancient cynicism — it describes a fundamental dynamic of social behavior.

**The fifth call to joy (v.15):** Each time Qoheleth recommends enjoyment, the context has gotten darker. Here, joy is commended immediately after observing that the righteous are treated like the wicked and vice versa. The joy is not denial — it is a conscious choice to embrace available good when the system cannot be understood or fixed.

*-- PNEUMA*
